title: Workers randomly stop serving tasks when scaling
body:
Hi,

I'm getting the following traceback:

```
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/celery/worker/worker.py", line 227, in _process_task
        req.execute_using_pool(self.pool)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/celery/worker/request.py", line 532, in execute_using_pool
        correlation_id=task_id,
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/celery/concurrency/base.py", line 155, in apply_async
        **options)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/billiard/pool.py", line 1494, in apply_async
        self._quick_put((TASK, (result._job, None, func, args, kwds)))
    TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/celery/worker/worker.py", line 227, in _process_task
        req.execute_using_pool(self.pool)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/celery/worker/request.py", line 532, in execute_using_pool
        correlation_id=task_id,
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/celery/concurrency/base.py", line 155, in apply_async
        **options)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.5/site-packages/billiard/pool.py", line 1494, in apply_async
        self._quick_put((TASK, (result._job, None, func, args, kwds)))
    TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable
```

This error is caused in a distributed environment, usually when I try to scale workers (run with 5+ workers). Workers after this error stop serving tasks and are just hanging.

Result backend is Redis, using RabbitMQ, Python3, serializer is JSON.

All tasks are configured with:
```
    ignore_result = False
    acks_late = True
    track_started = True
```

Workers are run with:
```
exec celery worker -A foo.start -Q queue1,queue2 -l debug --concurrency=1 --prefetch-multiplier=1 -Ofair
```

This traceback is not seen with eventlet, but workers still stop serving tasks:
```
exec celery worker -A foo.start -Q queue1,queue2 -l debug --concurrency=1 --prefetch-multiplier=1 -Ofair -P eventlet
```

Any help or suggestions?

Thanks!

## Checklist

- [*] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue.
      (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery
       version affected).
Affected Celery version:
  * Celery 4.0.0rc4
  * Celery 4.0.0rc6

Other Celery versions were not tested, master was not tested.

## Steps to reproduce

I don't have actual reproducer, workers stop working just randomly.

## Expected behavior

Workers should serve tasks as expected.

## Actual behavior

Randomly workers stop serving tasks - mostly during start up.
